requirements.statement: Project state is recorded as an append-only event log that is the single source of truth, from which all derived views are reconstructible.
requirements.rationale: Auditability is the product. A projection that cannot be rebuilt from its log is a claim, not a record.
acceptance: Every state transition appends exactly one line to .redgear/events.jsonl.
Replaying the log from line 0 reproduces task_graph.json byte-identically.
Event sequence numbers are gapless and strictly monotonic.
A gap or repeat in sequence numbers is reported as corruption and never auto-repaired.

requirements.statement: Work is modelled as a directed acyclic graph of tasks whose readiness is gated by verified dependencies.
requirements.rationale: Ordering is a correctness property, not a convenience. A task that runs before its dependency is verified produces work built on unproven foundations.
acceptance: A task is ready if and only if every hard dependency is in state verified.
A cycle in the edge set is rejected with the offending cycle named.
Every depends_on entry and edge endpoint refers to an existing node.
Readiness is recomputed after every transition and never cached across writes.

requirements.statement: Test authoring and implementation are separate task types with mutually exclusive write scopes, enforced by SHA-256 hashing of frozen paths.
requirements.rationale: An agent that can edit both the tests and the code they check is grading its own homework. The hash is what makes the separation mechanical rather than advisory.
acceptance: At claim time a SHA-256 digest is recorded for every file matching the task frozen globs.
Any modification, addition, or deletion inside a frozen glob fails verification before lint or tests run.
An implementation task carries no acceptance criteria of its own and inherits them from a verified test_authoring task.
Writable globs and frozen globs never overlap over the repository tracked file list.

requirements.statement: Task prompts are composed deterministically from task state by a pure function with no I/O, clock, or randomness.
requirements.rationale: The prompt is the entire interface between orchestrator knowledge and agent action. If it is not reproducible it cannot be reviewed, snapshotted, or debugged.
acceptance: Composing a prompt twice from identical state yields byte-identical output.
Section order is fixed and empty sections render as an explicit none rather than being omitted.
The prompt includes task identity, acceptance criteria, writable and frozen scope, applicable rules, the verification contract, and the outcome contract.
A retry prompt contains the formatted failure excerpt from the previous attempt.
Total prompt length never exceeds the configured character cap.

requirements.statement: Prompts are dispatched to an external coding agent CLI in non-interactive mode as a subprocess, with tool permissions constrained to the task scope.
requirements.rationale: Delegating execution keeps the orchestrator free of model credentials and lets the same engine drive any conforming CLI.
acceptance: Dispatch spawns the agent CLI with the prompt as an argv element, never interpolated into a shell string.
Allowed tools are derived from task scope and never include an unrestricted shell permission.
Permission-skipping flags are never passed under any configuration.
The exact argv is persisted for every dispatch with credential values redacted.
Standard output and standard error are captured to disk before parsing is attempted.

requirements.statement: Completed work is verified by six ordered gates computed locally by the orchestrator, short-circuiting on the first failure.
requirements.rationale: A verdict derived from anything the agent said is not a verdict. Only files and exit codes count.
acceptance: Gates run in the order scope, frozen hash, lint, tests, criteria coverage, coverage delta.
Gates after a failure are recorded as skipped and never omitted from the proof.
The changed file set is computed from git independently of any agent claim.
A mismatch between the agent declared file list and the real diff fails the scope gate.
For test authoring tasks the test gate passes only when the target tests fail.
Coverage is measured against changed lines only, never the whole repository.

requirements.statement: The orchestrator runs a continuous select, compose, dispatch, verify, decide loop until a defined terminal condition is reached.
requirements.rationale: Removing the human from the message relay is the entire point of the product.
acceptance: A verified task advances the graph and the loop immediately selects the next ready task.
A failed task returns to ready and is re-selected, producing a corrective prompt from the recorded failure.
The retry path uses the same code path as the first attempt with no conditional branch in the loop.
The loop terminates on exactly one of complete, stopped, blocked, budget exhausted, runner error, or engine error.
The termination reason is recorded and mapped to a distinct process exit code.

requirements.statement: The agent can declare itself blocked or under-scoped, which pauses the run for human intervention without consuming an attempt.
requirements.rationale: An agent whose only outcomes are pass and fail-and-retry is structurally incentivised to fake a pass when stuck. Honesty has to be free.
acceptance: The required structured result offers completed, blocked, and scope_insufficient as outcomes.
A blocked or scope_insufficient outcome leaves the attempt counter unchanged.
The prompt states explicitly that honest exit carries no penalty.
A blocked outcome ends the run with a distinct status and is never logged or displayed as a failure.

requirements.statement: Architecture decisions are recorded as immutable records carrying a machine-obeyable rule and a path scope, and matching rules are injected into future task prompts.
requirements.rationale: Decisions that live only in prose are documentation nobody reads. A rule bound to a path glob is a constraint the engine can enforce.
acceptance: An accepted record is never edited; a change is expressed by a new record that supersedes it.
Each record carries a single imperative rule sentence and at least one path glob.
Rules whose globs intersect a task writable scope appear verbatim in that task prompt.
A rule containing hedging language is rejected at validation time.

requirements.statement: A project plan is generated from a raw requirements document by a read-only agent dispatch, and cannot be executed until a human approves it.
requirements.rationale: The plan defines the tests, so a wrong plan produces confidently verified wrong software. It is the only unverified model output in the system and must be gated by a person.
acceptance: The planning dispatch is granted read-only tools and can never edit files.
A generated plan is written in draft state and the run command refuses to start on a draft plan.
Approval records the approver and the specification hash at time of approval.
Editing the specification after approval invalidates approval and requires re-approval.
Plan and run are separate commands with no flag that fuses them.

requirements.statement: A command line interface exposes initialisation, planning, approval, running, status, stopping, manual verification, projection rebuild, log inspection, and environment diagnosis.
requirements.rationale: The tool is distributed as a CLI; the command surface is the product boundary.
acceptance: Initialisation scaffolds the state directory and refuses to run outside a git repository.
Status reports task identity, type, state, attempt count, and blocking dependencies.
A dry run composes and prints every prompt without dispatching any of them.
Rebuild replays the log, compares against the on-disk projection, and fails loudly on divergence.
Diagnosis reports agent CLI version, harness command availability, and git cleanliness.

requirements.statement: A local read-only control plane renders the task graph, dispatched prompts, diffs, and verification proofs derived solely from the event log.
requirements.rationale: A reviewer must be able to see exactly what the orchestrator saw. A view that can display something the log does not support is not an audit trail.
acceptance: Every displayed fact is derived from the event log or a projection rebuilt from it.
The interface exposes no endpoint that mutates task state other than human approval actions.
Prompts are viewable verbatim as dispatched.
Verification proofs are viewable per task attempt including the raw diff.

requirements.statement: The orchestrator never calls a model API, never holds or reads a credential, and never opens a network socket.
requirements.rationale: This is what keeps the tool free to run, distributable without billing concerns, and safe to point at a private repository.
acceptance: No model provider client library appears in the dependency set.
No source file under the package reads an authentication environment variable.
No source file under the package imports a network client or socket module.
The parent environment may be propagated to the agent subprocess without being inspected.
Any value matching a credential-like name is redacted from every log line and event record.

requirements.statement: Every unattended run is bounded by hard caps and interruptible by an out-of-band stop signal.
requirements.rationale: An autonomous loop with file write and shell access and no ceiling is a dangerous object regardless of intent.
acceptance: Iteration count, wall clock duration, consecutive failure count, and per-dispatch turn count are all capped.
Caps are checked before each iteration begins and never mid-turn.
A stop sentinel file ends the run cleanly at the next iteration boundary.
Interrupt signals abort the current turn, terminate the agent process tree, and release all locks.
No termination path leaves an orphaned lock file.

requirements.statement: Content originating outside the trusted plan is contained within explicit delimiters and never treated as instruction.
requirements.rationale: Harness output can contain arbitrary text from any dependency in the tree, and it is being fed to an agent holding file write and shell permissions.
acceptance: Harness output, diff content, and source documents appear only inside labelled delimiters in the prompt body.
Delimiter markers occurring inside the content itself are escaped.
Untrusted content never reaches a system prompt append, a tool permission string, or any subprocess argument.
Terminal escape sequences are stripped and absolute paths are rewritten as repository-relative.

requirements.statement: All subprocess execution uses argument vectors without a shell, with timeouts, and with a scrubbed environment for harness commands.
requirements.rationale: Command injection through a prompt or a test name would compromise the machine running the loop.
acceptance: No call site enables shell interpretation.
Harness command vectors originate from configuration and never incorporate agent-supplied values.
Harness subprocesses receive an allowlisted environment that excludes credentials.
Every subprocess call has a timeout and a timeout is a recorded failure rather than an unhandled exception.
Timeouts terminate the whole process tree, not only the direct child.

requirements.statement: The codebase is fully type annotated and passes strict static type checking.
requirements.rationale: This is state-machine and parsing code where a type error is a corruption bug.
acceptance: Strict mode type checking passes across the package with no error suppressions.
No unparameterised container types and no dynamic escape hatches outside the canonical encoder.
Every external boundary parses into a validated model before use.

requirements.statement: The test suite is deterministic, requires no model, no agent CLI, and no network, and completes within ninety seconds.
requirements.rationale: A suite that needs a credential stops working the moment someone else clones the repository, and a suite that calls a model is not reproducible.
acceptance: No test invokes a real agent CLI or a model endpoint under any marker or condition.
Agent behaviour is simulated by a deterministic substitute that applies canned changes.
Verification gate tests run against a real git repository rather than mocked subprocess calls.
The full suite completes within ninety seconds on a standard development machine.

requirements.statement: All state file writes are atomic and no partially written state is ever observable.
requirements.rationale: A crash mid-write that leaves a truncated projection destroys the audit trail the product exists to provide.
acceptance: Every state file write goes to a temporary path, is flushed to disk, then atomically replaced.
The event log is opened in append mode and flushed before the appending call returns.
A proof directory is considered complete only when its verdict file is present.

requirements.statement: Agent CLI specifics are confined to a single adapter module behind a stable protocol.
requirements.rationale: Third-party CLI flags change between releases; coupling the loop to one vendor's surface guarantees breakage.
acceptance: The orchestrator and prompt composer are typed against a protocol and import no concrete adapter.
No module outside the adapter branches on which agent CLI is in use.
Each adapter records the CLI version it was verified against.

requirements.statement: The project maintains at least eighty-five percent line coverage over its own package.
requirements.rationale: A verification engine with poor self-coverage is not credible.
acceptance: Coverage measured over the package meets or exceeds eighty-five percent.
The coverage threshold is enforced in continuous integration as a hard failure.

requirements.statement: The tool targets Python 3.11 and above and installs as an isolated command line application.
requirements.rationale: Distribution as a single global command is the expected shape for a developer tool.
acceptance: The package declares a minimum Python version of 3.11.
Isolated installation from a built artifact yields a working command on a clean machine.
Packaging metadata is declared in the project file with no legacy setup script.

out_of_scope: Auto-committing, pushing, opening pull requests, merging, or deploying on behalf of the user
Concurrent or parallel agent execution across multiple tasks
Fully unattended planning without a human approval gate
Harness support for languages other than Python
Model routing, prompt-to-API calls, or any direct inference by the orchestrator
Sandboxing beyond subprocess isolation and tool permission allowlists
Authentication, user accounts, or role-based access control
Cost accounting presented as authoritative billing rather than estimate
Automatic recovery or repair of a divergent projection
